expectations.text: Uses all six CSF 2.0 functions including GOVERN (GV) — not the five-function 1.1 model
expectations.evidence: For each of the six functions (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover)... feeds Govern function, GV.OC

expectations.text: Distinguishes Current Profile vs Target Profile and gap analysis between them
expectations.evidence: you'll build a Current Profile (where you are today) and a Target Profile (where you want to be), then use the gap between them to drive your roadmap

expectations.text: References Implementation Tiers (1–4) as characterizing rigor of governance/risk practices, informing (not equaling) the target
expectations.evidence: Score using CSF Tiers (1-4: Partial, Risk Informed, Repeatable, Adaptive)... tiers describe how mature and integrated your risk management practices are... A common mistake is targeting Tier 4... across the board

expectations.text: Produces a prioritized action plan from the gaps (quick wins vs longer-term; owners/timelines)
expectations.evidence: document the specific gap, the remediation action, an owner, and a realistic timeline... sequencing quick wins (policy documentation, MFA rollout) ahead of larger capital/OT projects

expectations.text: Mentions using Community Profiles or Quick-Start Guides as accelerators where applicable
expectations.evidence: Use community/sector profiles where available as accelerators - NIST has published example profiles for some sectors
